title: What the River Carries
fact_notes: 架空の教材例・思考実験。実在の調査、統計、実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: In a hypothetical river valley, two villages are separated by a considerable distance, yet both depend on activities taking place along the same waterway.
sentences.ja: 仮想の河川流域で二つの村はかなり離れているが、どちらも同じ水路沿いの活動に依存している。

sentences.en: Residents of the upper village rarely visit the lower one, and each community has traditionally discussed its surroundings within the boundaries of its own settlement.
sentences.ja: 上流村の住民は下流村をめったに訪れず、各共同体は伝統的に自らの居住地の境界内で周辺環境を論じてきた。

sentences.en: A teacher asks students to imagine how the apparent separation of the two villages might disappear if they examined the region from the perspective of flowing water.
sentences.ja: 教師は流れる水の観点から地域を調べたら二つの村の見かけの分離がどう消えるか想像するよう求める。

sentences.en: The students initially concentrate on the channel itself, tracing its direction through the valley and marking the places where smaller streams enter it.
sentences.ja: 当初は川筋自体に集中し谷を通る方向をたどり小川が合流する場所を記す。

sentences.en: However, their map becomes increasingly complicated when they begin to consider activities occurring on land that is not immediately beside the river.
sentences.ja: しかし川のすぐそばではない土地での活動を考え始めると地図はますます複雑になる。

sentences.en: The group considers a fictional case in which a hillside is cleared for construction, leaving a large area of exposed soil during a period of heavy rain.
sentences.ja: 建設のため斜面が整地され大雨の時期に広範囲の土が露出する架空例を考える。

sentences.en: They discuss how material carried from this site might eventually reach a stream, even though the construction activity appears distant from the main river on an ordinary street map.
sentences.ja: 通常の道路地図では建設活動が本流から離れていても敷地から運ばれた物質が最終的に小川へ達し得ることを議論する。

sentences.en: Another hypothetical example concerns a garden that stores rainwater temporarily instead of allowing it to flow directly onto a paved surface.
sentences.ja: 別の仮想例は雨水を舗装面に直接流さず一時的に貯める庭に関する。

sentences.en: The students recognize that they cannot establish the effects of either arrangement without information about the actual terrain, weather conditions, and physical characteristics of the sites.
sentences.ja: 実際の地形、気象条件、敷地の物理的特徴の情報なく効果は確定できないと認識する。

sentences.en: The teacher introduces the idea of organizing their investigation around the area from which water drains toward a shared location rather than relying exclusively on administrative boundaries.
sentences.ja: 行政境界だけに頼らず共通地点へ水が流れ込む範囲を中心に調査する考えを教師が紹介する。

sentences.en: This alternative perspective encourages the students to investigate relationships between locations that would appear unrelated if the region were divided solely according to the responsibilities of different local authorities.
sentences.ja: この別の観点は異なる自治体の責任によってのみ地域を区切れば無関係に見える場所間の関係を調べるよう促す。

sentences.en: They prepare a diagram indicating possible connections without claiming that the diagram accurately predicts the movement of every substance under every combination of circumstances.
sentences.ja: あらゆる事情の組み合わせで全物質の移動を正確に予測するとは主張せず可能なつながりを示す図を作る。

sentences.en: The exercise reveals why identifying an appropriate geographical scale is an important part of defining an environmental question.
sentences.ja: 適切な地理的尺度の特定が環境上の問いを定義する重要部分である理由を示す。

sentences.en: During a discussion with imaginary village representatives, the students discover that a shared environmental concern does not necessarily imply identical priorities.
sentences.ja: 架空の村代表との議論で共通の環境懸念が同じ優先事項を意味するとは限らないと知る。

sentences.en: One community may have limited resources for changing existing practices, whereas another may have more immediate reasons to investigate possible consequences further downstream.
sentences.ja: 一方は既存慣行変更の資源が限られ、他方は下流の潜在的影響をより緊急に調べる理由があるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The groups discuss which information each community would need to understand the concerns of the other and which questions would require investigation beyond the scope of their classroom activity.
sentences.ja: 互いの懸念を理解するため必要な情報と教室活動の範囲外の調査を要する問いを議論する。

sentences.en: They avoid treating the imagined discussion as evidence that any actual environmental intervention would produce a particular result.
sentences.ja: 仮想議論を実際の環境介入が特定結果を生む証拠とは扱わない。

sentences.en: Environmental problems can be difficult to describe when the relevant physical processes extend beyond the boundaries through which people ordinarily organize their responsibilities.
sentences.ja: 関連物理過程が通常責任を組織する境界を超えると環境問題は記述しにくくなる場合がある。

sentences.en: A useful map can make some of those connections visible, but its value depends on how carefully its assumptions are distinguished from observations supported by evidence.
sentences.ja: 有益な地図はつながりを可視化できるが、前提と根拠ある観察をどれほど注意深く区別するかに価値が依存する。

sentences.en: Cooperation consequently involves not only agreeing to pursue a common objective but also determining which relationships must be understood before the objective can meaningfully guide decisions.
sentences.ja: 協力には共通目標の追求に合意するだけでなく目標が意味ある判断指針になる前に理解すべき関係を特定することも伴う。

sentences.en: The fictional valley illustrates how changing the boundaries of an investigation may change the kinds of questions that people consider worth asking about the environment.
sentences.ja: 架空流域は調査境界を変えると環境について問う価値があると考える問いの種類も変わり得ることを示す。

vocabulary.definition: action taken to influence a situation

options: Their dependence on the same waterway.

questions.prompt: Why does the map become more complicated?
options: Every stream was removed from the map.
Activities away from the channel may still be relevant to the river.
The students could no longer identify the river.
questions.explanation_ja: 離れた土地の活動も関係する。

options: Planting a garden beside a shop.
Measuring the depth of the river.

questions.prompt: Why cannot the effects of the arrangements be established immediately?
options: All rainwater moves at identical speeds.
They depend on site-specific physical and weather conditions.

questions.prompt: What geographical perspective does the teacher introduce?
options: A map divided by population alone.
An area from which water drains toward a shared location.
A list of unrelated administrative offices.
A survey of individual houses only.
questions.explanation_ja: 共通地点への集水範囲。

options: It proves all communities have identical responsibilities.
It removes the need for observations.
It reveals connections that administrative divisions may conceal.
questions.explanation_ja: 行政区分で見えない関係。

questions.prompt: Why may the villages have different priorities?
options: They do not share any environmental concern.
Their resources and exposure to possible consequences differ.
One village has no relation to the river.

questions.prompt: What did the groups avoid claiming?
options: That an imagined discussion proves actual intervention outcomes.
That further investigation might be needed.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の効果の証明ではない。

options: Local boundaries define all environmental processes.
A map alone can predict the effects of any action.
Environmental inquiry should consider physical connections that extend beyond administrative boundaries.
A shared river guarantees identical priorities.
questions.explanation_ja: 物理的つながりと行政境界。
